drills.q: Name the eight labs defining the 2026 frontier and one structural fact about how families ship.
drills.a: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI (closed-first); DeepSeek, Qwen/Alibaba, Mistral, Meta (open-weight/transition). Structural: every family ships a tier ladder — flagship/workhorse/fast — spanning ~$1.25-$50/M output tokens, with reasoning-effort dials and ~1M-token contexts.

drills.q: List the five model-card audit lenses from memory.
drills.a: EVALS (cited vs omitted, vendor vs independent, tier, precision), DATA (sources, cutoff, contamination method), LICENSE (OSI status, thresholds, carve-outs, incorporated policies, output rights), SAFETY (red-team scope + residual-risk owner), OPERATIONS (pinning, static notices, output ceilings, emissions).

drills.q: A teammate calls a Llama-class model 'open source.' Correct them precisely.
drills.a: It's open-weight, not open source: the Community License fails OSI's definition per OSI's own analysis — purpose restrictions via AUP, user-class discrimination (700M MAU provision), field-of-endeavor limits, EU carve-outs in some versions. MIT/Apache 2.0 convey actual open-source freedoms; community licenses convey revocable privileges with silent-update risk.

drills.q: Quote three contamination statistics that justify distrusting raw public benchmark numbers.
drills.a: ~29.1% of MMLU items flagged contaminated (JHU NAACL 2024); C-Eval ~45.8%; multilingual benchmarks up to ~91.8%. Supporting: Meta self-reported 16% MMLU overlap for Llama 2; GPT-4 report admitted 9/34 exams >20% overlap; clean mirrors drop GSM8K ~13 points; ITD removes ~22.9% of MMLU inflation.

drills.q: Why do n-gram decontamination filters miss leaks, and what actually works?
drills.a: Exact-match filters (13-gram GPT-3 era, 40-gram GPT-4) can't catch paraphrases, translations, or reformatted tables — the dominant multilingual leak path (~92% contamination). Works better: dynamic benchmarks refreshed from post-cutoff sources (LiveBench), private held-out sets (MMLU-CF), and inference-time decontamination.

drills.q: A card shows great scores but you'll deploy int8 quantization. What's the issue and the fix?
drills.a: The bf16-vs-deployed precision gap: Llama 4's card explicitly evaluates on bf16 while shipping quantized checkpoints — published numbers don't describe your artifact. Fix: demand precision-matched evaluations from the vendor or run your own quantized-model eval on your private set before committing the serving configuration.

drills.q: Your product serves EU users. Which license lens items fire during teardown?
drills.a: Jurisdictional carve-outs first — certain Llama license versions explicitly restricted EU-based users; then AUP incorporated-by-reference (updatable terms), attribution mechanics for distribution pipelines, and data-provenance disclosures mapping to GDPR duties. This is exactly why license review gates pilots rather than launches.

drills.q: Mid-2026 saw a flagship suspended 22 days by export controls and another gated 12 days for government review. What do you change Monday morning?
drills.a: Treat regulatory state as an availability dimension: test (not merely document) multi-vendor fallback quarterly, keep the abstraction layer, wire regulatory monitoring into ops alerting, pin snapshot IDs with rotation diffs, and allocate suspension risk in vendor contracts. The trigger is policy; the blast radius is engineering readiness.

drills.q: Vendor reports SOTA but discloses no contamination methodology and no independent reproductions. Walk your assessment.
drills.a: Treat numbers as unverified upper bounds: check third-party indexes (disclosure ranges 8/8 down to 0/8 across majors), run private task evals, consult dynamic-benchmark standings, ask the vendor directly for filter sizes and overlap stats. Silence where peers disclose is itself decision-relevant disclosure-quality information.

drills.q: Contrast DeepSeek vs Meta openness strategies and extract the durable lesson.
drills.a: DeepSeek: consistent MIT licensing of frontier MoE flagships + R-reasoners with published recipes — openness as strategy that reset pricing globally. Meta: openness as instrument — Llama under a non-OSI Community License seeded an ecosystem, then frontier pivoted closed before partial Apache reopenings. Durable lesson: openness is a per-model LICENSE property, not a lab identity; audit every model, trust no lineage.

drills.q: CFO asks why comparable-capability models vary ~40x in price. Answer without hand-waving.
drills.a: Positioning margin vs volume tiers; inference structure (MoE active params, reasoning-token burn at effort tiers); bundling of managed safety/SLAs/compliance; strategic anchoring — MIT competitors floor pricing near $1.25/M while capability-at-any-price buyers sustain $50/M premiums; market immaturity means price moves faster than value evidence. Decision rule: price-per-task at your quality bar from your private eval.

drills.q: What map-redraw signals should trigger a portfolio review?
drills.a: Simultaneous multi-lab flagship releases within a month (repricing follows); any lab changing disclosure patterns (strategy shifts precede products); suspension/gating/regulatory events; license-family changes within a lineage; and quarterly incumbent-vs-challenger drift on YOUR private eval even absent external events.
